channel.title: Elsewhere · Reading
channel.description: Other writers, other papers — open the link. A curated shelf of no-paywall original space writing the desk is pointing at. Preview only; read the piece at the source.

item.title: An obsessively linked rundown of recent global lunar exploration
item.description: Moon Monday #292 — Chang’e 7 slips to next year, Griffin and FLIP still in the 2026 queue, Artemis II heat-shield review, and three more Artemis Accords signatories.

item.title: Where Your Elements Came From
item.description: September 14 picture: hydrogen from the Big Bang, carbon and oxygen from stellar fusion — a periodic table of how the atoms in you were made.

item.title: Could clues to ancient alien civilizations hide in a bucket of Moon dust?
item.description: SETI Institute researchers argue the lunar surface is a long-term collector of artifacts — not because anyone lived there, but because the Moon keeps what hits it.

item.title: Venus moon would have been doomed from the start
item.description: New paper: a captured or impact-formed satellite around Venus would not have lasted. The planet’s spin and tides do not leave room for a durable moon.

item.title: Vol 45, Week 37 — this week in space
item.description: The open weekly ledger: Progress MS-35 to station, UKIRT winding down, JUICE Earth flyby on the 25th, Crew-13 later in the month. Week 38 not posted yet.

item.title: A new surface atlas of Phobos will help JAXA’s MMX mission collect its samples
item.description: Planetary science for the sample-return: a map of the potato moon so MMX can pick a safe scoop.

item.title: China is building a lunar navigation and communications network
item.description: Moon Monday #291 — Jatan Mehta walks through each piece China has demonstrated toward a Queqiao-class lunar navcom stack, including Earth–Moon laser links.

item.title: What’s up in the night sky: September 2026
item.description: Crescent Moon with Venus on the 14th, Antares on the 17th, equinox on the 23rd, Harvest Moon on the 26th.
